presentation.label: Any track to MAIN, CUE or PHONES
presentation.summary: Turn the headphone jack into a third assignable output pair and pick each track's outputs with CUE + LEVEL.
presentation.overview: Adds MATRIX beside NORMAL and STUDIO in PROJECT > CONTROL > AUDIO (the box stock calls CUE CFG, titled OUT CFG with the module). In MATRIX, LEVEL sets a track's level and CUE + LEVEL chooses where it plays: MAIN, CUE or PHONES as stereo pairs in any combination, or a single mono jack of the six (track L+R summed at half each, so a centred sound keeps its level). The choice is stored in the Part, so it survives SRC page resets, Part reload and project save. The MIXER's MIX knob becomes the PHONES output level. Inputs keep their stock DIR routing to MAIN.
highlights: Three stereo output pairs: MAIN, CUE and the headphone jack.
Per track: any combination of MAIN, CUE and PHONES, or one mono jack (MAIN L/R, CUE L/R, PHONES L/R).
Routing lives in the Part: SRC page resets and track clears leave it alone.
With MASTER TRACK on, tracks routed to MAIN feed the master and track 8's destination picks where the master plays.
usage: PROJECT > CONTROL > AUDIO: select OUT CFG > MATRIX and press YES.
On a track, the LEV box is labelled with the destination (MN, PHN, ...). Hold CUE and turn LEVEL to change it.
In the MIXER, MIX (labelled PHN) sets the PHONES output level. Choose NORMAL or STUDIO again to return to stock behaviour.

limitations: Builds with the stock DSP code built in and takes a given-up stock effect's program memory on core 0. The builder chooses it: SPRING REV first, then PLATE REV or DARK REV when other modules also need room. The given-up effect leaves the FX2 menu.
The MATRIX mixdown costs core 0 up to about 208 more instructions per sample than stock (every track on ALL, MASTER on, bus levels moving); every track on MAIN adds about 20.
Switching to or from MATRIX rewrites every Part's LEVEL and cue bytes (and, into NORMAL, the project's cue settings) by documented rules; save to keep it.
A MATRIX project opened on a stock OS loads as STUDIO with tiny cue levels; switch to NORMAL or STUDIO before flashing another OS.
Changes core 0's mixdown and headphone crossfade; other modules that hook those sites are refused by the ledger.
Not yet combinable with Analog BD, whose builder places DSP code only beside a reviewed list of effects.

resources.recorded: Measured in the ColdFire port (instructions) and from the build report

storage.label: Memory
storage.display: 1,678 B DRAM + 671 DSP P words + 193 DSP Y words
storage.conditions: ColdFire unit .text 1,532 B and .data 146 B (m68k-elf-as section sizes of matrix.s); DSP P code 657 words and a 14-word table in SPRING REV's harvested span on core 0 (727 + 42 before 0.1.1); DSP Y $c00..$cc0. No per-track copies, no audio buffers.

processing.label: DSP core 0 mixdown
processing.conditions: Executed instructions of the mixdown (P:$257..$2d5) and headphone crossfade (P:$30a..$35a) per 16-sample frame, every track on ALL, MASTER on, MAIN/CUE/PHONES levels moving, including the frame that rebuilds the routing lists: 4,194 + 192 per frame, rounded up per sample (0.1.0: 4,240 + 192; 4,336 before the 12-word trim, TESTING.md). Stock: 880 + 191. Cycles and bus stalls are not modelled.

impact.conditions: Eight tracks in MATRIX at the dearest routing (every track on ALL, MASTER on, levels moving); NORMAL and STUDIO run stock code plus a 4-instruction check.

cpu.rationale: The level-page detour runs once a frame, 189 instructions typical and 229 at most (all eight tracks changing destination). The mode conversion runs once per switch in the UI task.

dsp.rationale: Up to about 208 extra instructions per sample on core 0 (about 7% of 3,120); about 20 with every track on MAIN.

memory.rationale: 1,678 bytes of DRAM code and data, 671 DSP program words reused from SPRING REV and 193 DSP Y words.

tests.summary: The image gate passes 117 checks under the ColdFire port: every destination, mono sums, MAIN against stock, the level law, MKII, MASTER, mute, DIR, the declick, every mode-conversion rule by the keys (including track 8 as the master and the power-cycle copies), CC 51 out and a power cycle. On an MKII the author tested routing, levels, the MIXER, everyday flows, saving and power and the conversion (functional report, 7–9 Oct 2026). No timed stress run, no chip timing. 0.1.1 over USB on the MKII (RAM-booted beta base, 16 Oct 2026): MATRIX on and off, the always-on LEV label, routing to MAIN, CUE, PHONES, a mono jack and OFF, and the PHONES level all passed and, on the flashed base, a power cycle kept MATRIX, the routing and the module set (the LEV box needed a redraw).

conditions.parameterExtremes: Every destination code 0..13 per track, all eight tracks on ALL, mixed stereo and mono routings, MAIN/CUE/PHONES levels 0..127, MASTER on and off.
conditions.parameterModulation: MAIN, CUE and MIX levels changed every other frame for 60 frames; LEVEL, XVOL scenes, locks and LFOs act through stock gain ramps the mixdown reads, unchanged.
conditions.modeSwitching: All eight tracks changing destination in one frame (list rebuild and declick), and NORMAL/STUDIO/MATRIX switches.
conditions.maxLoad: One instance per unit (a global mode). Worst measured: 4,194 + 192 executed instructions per 16-sample frame on core 0, every track on ALL with MASTER on; stock 880 + 191.
conditions.inputConditions: Tone and four-input test audio; the code path does not depend on sample values. Counts are executed instructions, not modelled cycles.

conditions.parameterExtremes: Every destination per track, levels 0..127, MASTER on and off.
conditions.parameterModulation: Level changes every other frame; not routed through LFOs or locks.
conditions.modeSwitching: All eight tracks changing destination in one frame (the declick path for each).
conditions.maxLoad: The level-page detour, once a frame: 189 executed instructions typical, 229 at most. Budget: 10% of a 362.8 us frame at 266 MHz. The mode conversion (16 banks x 8 Parts) runs once per switch in the UI task, outside the frame.
conditions.inputConditions: Independent of audio. Executed instructions; cycles and cache effects are not modelled.

regions.name: ColdFire code and the AUDIO page tables stock code points at (DRAM unit .text)
ColdFire data: routing state and names (DRAM unit .data)
DSP core 0 program: mixdown and phones hooks, in SPRING REV's harvested span
DSP core 0 program: the 14-word destination table (3 codes a word)
DSP core 0 Y: bus factors, lists, PHONES buffer ($c00..$cc0)

memory.conditions: From the static build's runtime ELF and the DSP placement report. Detours patch stock instructions in place; the level-page words and battery-RAM copies the module uses are stock's. No heap; ColdFire stack use is the callers' frames plus at most 48 bytes (set_mode's saved registers and the conversion's call chain).

hardware.summary: Over USB on an Octatrack MKII: a RAM-booted beta base built from this source (identity 3e3e3de1..., MAIN 5ca0afbf...) with the 0.1.1 package (e2df2fbf...) installed by trial, rollback and then trial and keep. The author checked: the switch into MATRIX and back to NORMAL, the always-on destination label in the LEV box, CUE + LEVEL routing to MAIN, CUE, PHONES, a mono jack and OFF on a playing track with the audio where the label says, and MIX as the PHONES level. All passed. Then flashed the same base: with MATRIX selected and a track on MNL, a power cycle restored all seven installed modules, MATRIX and the routing; the LEV box first showed stock's split bars until CUE redrew it.
limitations: One power cycle on the flashed base; no project save and reload or Part reload on this version over USB. After the power cycle the LEV box showed stock's split bars until CUE redrew the page (display only; routing was right).
Output Matrix alone on the base; MASTER TRACK, STUDIO, conversions in other Parts and banks and CC 51 out not checked on the unit for this version.
Checked by ear; no audio recording or chip timing. The smaller DSP code's identical output is shown in the emulator only.
The first trial's rollback was refused once (needs-recovery) and completed by the base without a further command.

tutorial.title: Quick tutorial
steps: Press PROJ, open CONTROL > AUDIO, move right into OUT CFG, select MATRIX and press YES.
Select track 1, hold CUE and turn LEVEL until the LEV box reads PHN: track 1 now plays only in the headphones.
Open the MIXER and turn MIX (PHN) to set the headphone level; choose NORMAL again to return to stock routing.

access.location: PROJECT > CONTROL > AUDIO > OUT CFG (stock CUE CFG) > MATRIX; then CUE + LEVEL on any audio track, and MIX in the MIXER.
steps: Include Output Matrix in your build.
Press PROJ (MKII), open CONTROL > AUDIO, move right into the OUT CFG box, select MATRIX and press YES.
Select an audio track, hold CUE and turn LEVEL to pick its outputs; the LEV box's label always shows the destination.
Open the MIXER: MIX, labelled PHN, sets the headphone output level.
